findings.title: Promised data/code are not actually provided; primary statistics not reproducible from shipped materials
findings.evidence: Paper sections 2.1/2.2/Discussion state 'Data are provided in the Supplementary Materials' (paper_extracted.txt lines ~234, ~523-525). OSF node e285f backing the preprint is public but contains exactly one file, the supplement PDF jcm-09-03350-s001 (2).pdf (SHA256 57B61722...); 0 children; no raw participant data, no raw item responses, no JASP 0.14 output, no WEKA 3.9 arff/models, no analysis code. Consequently Tables 1-2 regression coefficients, R^2=0.103/0.356, F-change, and Table 3 ML metrics cannot be independently recomputed (marked not-checkable-without-raw-data).
findings.why_it_matters: The primary inferential claims (two multiple regressions and the headline ML sensitivity ~0.76) rest entirely on data that were described as available but were not shipped in any raw or code form. A reader cannot reproduce the headline results.
findings.fix: Upload the de-identified participant-level dataset (raw item responses + derived 18 variables), plus the JASP .jasp analysis files and WEKA 3.9 .arff pipelines/configuration, to the OSF project (node e285f) referenced by the DOI; add a README describing the derivation chain raw -> derived -> analysis.

findings.title: Supplement Table S2 Item 1 group means are inconsistent with its own reported t and Cohen's d
findings.evidence: Reported means 2.62 (SD 0.91, high) vs 1.84 (SD 0.91, low), n=393/1642. Pooled two-sample t recomputes to 15.263 and |d| to 0.857, but manuscript reports t=27.950 and |d|=1.57. The reported t and d are mutually consistent both with each other (t=|d|*17.807) and with a mean difference of ~1.43 points, i.e. roughly double the table's printed 0.78-point difference. Items 2-10 in the same table are all internally consistent, ruling out a global extraction/alignment artifact.
findings.why_it_matters: Item-level PSS-10 analysis is a secondary exhibit, not a primary hypothesis test; however the inconsistency is not explained by the data and undermines confidence in the table.
findings.fix: Re-check the raw data for Item 1 means/SDs (or the Item 1 t/d). Correct whichever side is wrong so that means, t and d agree within rounding.

findings.title: Sign convention of Cohen's d in Table S2
findings.evidence: All ten items print negative d while the recomputed magnitude uses (M_high - M_low)/SDpool, i.e. d is reported under a low-minus-high convention. This is internally consistent across items and does not change conclusions, but the convention is not stated in the table; a reader assumes high-minus-low.
findings.why_it_matters: Documenting the sign convention prevents misinterpretation of whether higher stress maps to positive or negative d.
findings.fix: State the d convention in the Table S2 legend or report d with consistent sign relative to the direction of the difference.

findings.title: Abstract overstates best sensitivity ('greater than 76%')
findings.evidence: Table 3 best high-stress sensitivity = 0.759 (Logistic), i.e. 75.9%, which is NOT greater than 76%; the Discussion correctly says sensitivity 'approaching 0.759'. Also all four classifiers ROC 0.697-0.782 is consistent with '0.70-0.78'.
findings.why_it_matters: Minor wording overstatement in the headline abstract figure.
findings.fix: Restate abstract as 'sensitivity approaching 76%' or give the exact 0.759.

findings.title: Education-mean drift between paper text and supplement
findings.evidence: paper_extracted.txt section 2.2 reports education 15.35 (SD 3.43); supplement Table S1 all-participants reports 15.36 (SD 3.43).
findings.why_it_matters: Trivial descriptive inconsistency between the two shipped sources.
